newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha slips with crude, arb still attractive.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha slips with crude, arb still attractive.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices edged lower on Monday, tracking a crude selloff after news that Iraq said it had agreed to all U.N. conditions that held up implementation of the oil-for-food-deal, traders said.
Iraqi U.N. ambassador Nizar Hamdoon predicted oil could start flowing in December.
Some traders still believed naphtha was well supported by an open arbitrage to the U.S. that sucked about 100,000-150,000 tonnes out of Europe last week.
But NWE as a whole was still seen relatively balanced, with smaller Russian and Algerian cargoes available this month.
"Propane (in the U.S.) has been strong for about two months, it's the arb that has kicked things up again," said one trader, who described his opinion on prices as "constructive."
No further physical deals were heard today and traders warned prices may correct some of last week's sharp gains if the U.S. buying lightens up temporarily.
Dec swaps ended down $1 at $224.50/$225.50 with Jan holding a $7.50 backwardation at $217/$218.
NWE cargoes fell notionally $2 to $226/$228 cif.

Crude futures fell slightly on the Iraq news but soon trimmed some of those losses. OPEC ministers are meeting this week in Vienna and are widely expected to roll over the output ceiling of 25.03 million barrels per day.

Hamdoon was in New York for talks with Undersecretary-General Chinmaya Gharekhan, who heads a U.N. task force overseeing the deal that would allow the sale of $2 billion of Iraqi oil over six months on a renewable basis.

The naphtha to crude crack spread has narrowed slightly in recent sessions, to about $48 on Friday from $55 on Nov 6. But the crack still remains above its mean price over the last two years of $38 a tonne.
